How did scientists first notice that electricity creates magnetism?

In 1820, Hans Christian Oersted saw a compass needle move near a wire carrying electric current!
copy.tl:
Paano unang napansin ng mga siyentipiko na ang kuryente ay gumagawa ng magnetismo?

Noong 1820, nakita ni Hans Christian Oersted na gumalaw ang karayom ng kompas malapit sa kawad na may kuryente!

Unsaon pagmahayag sa mga siyentipiko nga ang kuryente mohimo ug magnetismo?

Niadtong 1820, nakita ni Hans Christian Oersted nga molihok ang karayom sa kompas duol sa kawad nga adunay kuryente!

copy.en: An electromagnet is a magnet made by electricity, so it can grab iron and drop it when the power is switched off!
copy.tl: Ang elektromagnet ay magneto na gawa sa kuryente, kaya kaya nitong humila ng bakal at bitiwan ito kapag pinatay ang kuryente!
copy.bis: Ang elektromagneto usa ka magneto nga hinimo sa kuryente, busa makakabig kini sa puthaw ug mobitaw kung patyon ang kuryente!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The north and south poles switch places!

copy.en:
What happens if you reverse the current in an electromagnet?

The north and south poles switch places! It's like the magnet does a quick flip.
copy.tl:
Anong mangyayari kapag binaligtad mo ang kuryente sa elektromagnet?

Nagpapalitan ang hilaga at timog na polo! Parang nag-flip ang magnet.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung balihon nimo ang kuryente sa elektromagnet?

Mag-ilis ang amihanan ug habagatang polo! Murag nag-flip ang magnet.

copy.en:
Why do electromagnets use soft iron for their core?

Soft iron becomes a magnet super fast when current flows, but loses its magnetism just as quickly when you switch it off!
copy.tl:
Bakit malambot na bakal ang ginagamit bilang ubod ng elektromagnet?

Mabilis itong nagiging magnet kapag may kuryente, at mabilis ding mawalan nito kapag pinatay!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga humok nga puthaw ang giyamit isip ubod sa elektromagnet?

Paspas kining mahimong magnet kung naay kuryente, ug paspas sad mawala ang pagka-magnet kung palongon!

copy.en: Want a stronger electromagnet? Just add more turns of wire or send more current flowing through it to boost its power!
copy.tl: Gusto mo ng mas malakas na electromagnet? Dagdagan lang ang ikot ng alambre o damihan ang kuryenteng dumadaloy para lumakas ito!
copy.bis: Gusto ka ba ug mas mokusog nga electromagnet? Dugangi lang ug likos sa alambre o daghani ug kuryente para mokusog kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The electromagnet loses its magnetism!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties

copy.en:
What happens when you turn off the electric current?

The electromagnet loses its magnetism! This means you can easily switch it on and off.
copy.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kapag pinatay mo ang electric current?

Nawawala ang magnetism ng electromagnet! Kaya naman madali mo itong ma-on at ma-off.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung palongon nimo ang electric current?

Mawala ang magnetism sa electromagnet! Busa sayon nimo kini ma-on ug ma-off.

copy.bis: Ilha ang electron! Kining gamay nga subatomic particle sa sulod sa atom kanunay adunay negatibong charge.

copy.bis: Ang mga electron molihok nga paspas kaayo palibot sa nucleus, mao nga sama sa panganod ang ilang dagway!

Where do electrons hang out in an atom?

They don't stay still! Electrons move around the outside of the atom's nucleus.

Saan nag-iistay ang mga electron sa isang atom?

Hindi sila nakatigil! Ang mga electron ay umiikot sa palibot ng nucleus ng atom.
copy.bis:
Asa nagpuyo ang mga electron sa usa ka atom?

Dili sila nagpabilin! Ang mga electron nagtuyok sa gawas sa nucleus sa atom.

copy.en:
How does an LED make light?

An LED is a semiconductor device! When current flows through its p-n junction, electrons fill 'holes' and release energy as visible light.
copy.tl:
Paano gumagawa ng liwanag ang LED?

Ang LED ay isang semiconductor device! Kapag dumaan ang kuryente sa p-n junction nito, ang mga elektron ay sumasakop ng 'butas' at naglalabas ng enerhiya bilang ilaw.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa LED og suga?

Ang LED usa ka semiconductor device! Inig-agos sa kuryente sa p-n junction niini, ang mga elektron magpuno sa mga 'buho' ug maglabas ug enerhiya ingon nakita nga suga.

copy.en:
How do we protect an LED from too much power?

We use Ohm's law to find the right resistor! For a 9 V battery and an LED needing 2 V at 20 mA, we need 350 ohms of resistance.
copy.tl:
Paano natin poprotektahan ang isang LED?

Ginagamit natin ang Ohm's law para sa tamang resistor! Kung 9 V ang baterya at kailangan ng LED ng 2 V sa 20 mA, kailangan natin ng 350 ohms na resistance.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-protect sa LED?

Gigamit nato ang Ohm's law para sa husto nga resistor! Kung 9 V ang baterya ug kinahanglan sa LED ug 2 V sa 20 mA, kinahanglan nato ug 350 ohms nga resistance.

copy.en:
How do we protect LEDs from too much current?

We use a resistor! It adds resistance to a circuit to control the current, protecting LEDs and other sensitive components.
copy.tl:
Paano natin poprotektahan ang mga LED sa masyadong malaking kuryente?

Gumagamit tayo ng resistor! Nagdadagdag ito ng resistensya sa circuit para kontrolin ang kuryente at protektahan ang mga LED at sensitive na component.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagprotekta sa mga LED gikan sa kapin kaayo nga kuryente?

Muggamit kita og resistor! Nagdugang kini og resistensya sa circuit aron kontrolon ang kuryente ug protektahan ang mga LED ug sensitibong component.

copy.tl: Ang thermistor ay isang temperature sensor na nagbabago ng resistensya ayon sa temperatura. Tumutulong ito sa mga thermostat ng aircon at ibang device para makontrol ang temperatura ng silid!
copy.bis: Ang thermistor usa ka temperature sensor nga nagbag-o sa resistensya sumala sa temperatura. Kini nagtabang sa mga thermostat sa aircon ug ubang device aron makontrol ang temperatura sa kwarto!

How do elements make compounds?

Two or more elements combine to form a compound, like hydrogen and oxygen forming water!

Dalawa o higit pang elemento ang nagsasama para bumuo ng compound, gaya ng hydrogen at oxygen na gumagawa ng tubig!

Unsaon paghimo sa compound ang mga elemento?

Duha o sobra pa ka elemento magtipon aron maporma ang compound, sama sa hydrogen ug oxygen nga naghimo og tubig!

What are an elephant's tusks really?

An elephant's long tusks are actually very large teeth.

Ang mahahabang pangil ng elepante ay talagang napakalalaking ngipin.
copy.bis:
Unsa gyud ang bangkil sa elepante?

Ang taas nga bangkil sa elepante mao gyud ang dagko kaayong ngipon.

A huge elephant's heart beats only about 30 times a minute, while a tiny shrew's heart beats hundreds of times!

Kinsay mas paspas mopitik ang kasingkasing: elepante o shrew?

Ang kasingkasing sa dakong elepante mopitik og mga 30 ka beses lang kada minuto, samtang ang shrew gatosan!

copy.bis: Ang tanang electromagnetic wave, gikan sa radio hangtod sa gamma, mobiyahe sa vacuum sa managsamang katulin! Mao na ang katulin sa kahayag, nga mga 300,000 ka kilometro kada segundo.

How do Philippine power plants make electricity?

They all use the same trick! Steam or water spins a turbine, rotating a magnet inside wire coils to generate electricity.

Paano gumagawa ng kuryente ang mga power plant sa Pilipinas?

Pareho lang ang sikreto nila! Ang singaw o tubig ay nagpapalikot ng turbine, na nagpapaiikot ng magnet sa loob ng wire coils para gumawa ng kuryente.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo ug kuryente sa mga power plant sa Pilipinas?

Parehas ra ang ilang sekreto! Ang singaw o tubig nagpalikot sa turbine, nga nagpailikot sa magnet sulod sa wire coils aron magmugna ug kuryente.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why does a generator get harder to spin when it's making electricity?

copy.en:
Why does a generator get harder to spin when it's making electricity?

Lenz's law says the induced current in a coil always opposes the change that caused it! You must push harder to spin a generator when it delivers current — that's conservation of energy!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas nahihirapan paikutin ang generator kapag gumagawa ito ng kuryente?

Sabi ng batas ni Lenz, ang induced current sa coil ay palaging tumatanggihan ang pagbabago na nagdulot nito! Kailangan mong pilitan nang mas malakas ang generator — iyan ang conservation of energy!
copy.bis:
Ngano mas lisod paliduson ang generator kung naghatag kini og kuryente?

Naa kini sa tunga sa infrared ug ultraviolet!

Ito ay isang transverse wave na gawa sa nagbabagong electric field at magnetic field na naglalakbay nang patayo sa direksyon ng alon!

Ang endangered na hayop ay buhay pa pero kakaunti na at maaari pang iligtas. Ang extinct ay wala nang buhay na natitira — nawala na magpakailanman.

Nahibalo ba ka nga ang enerhiya pwedeng magtago o molihok?

Adunay enerhiyang gitipigan ug andam na, sama sa baterya! Aduna usab nga naglihok na, sama sa init, kahayag, ug tingog.

Ang El Niño at La Niña ay magkasalungat na yugto ng ENSO! Dito, nagbabago ang temperatura ng tubig sa Pasipiko at ang hanging ekwador.

copy.tl: Ang mga organismo ay naninirahan sa mga lugar kung saan sila makakakuha ng pagkain at makakarami, at ang iba ay dumarami kapag ang kapaligiran ay naging mas angkop para sa kanilang life cycle.
copy.bis: Ang mga organismo nagpuyo sa mga lugar diin sila makakuha sa pagkaon ug makadaghan, ug ang uban modaghan kon ang kalikopan mahimong mas angay alang sa ilang life cycle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During severe drought, some animals like snails enter a sleep-like state called estivation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: Estivation is a behavioral/physiological response to drought, not an example of animals having 'changed to better suit their environment' in the sense of evolutionary adaptation (mimicry/camouflage). The card does not use secondary sources and does not describe a change in the animal, only a temporary state.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: saving water and energy until the rain returns
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions saving water, which relates to a basic need (water), but it does not identify basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) as a concept. It only describes one behavior in one animal, not the general needs of all living things.

copy.en:
What do snails do during a severe drought?

During severe drought, some animals like snails enter a sleep-like state called estivation, saving water and energy until the rain returns.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng snail sa matinding tagtuyot?

Sa panahon ng matinding tagtuyot, ang ilang hayop tulad ng snail ay pumapasok sa parang pagtulog na tinatawag na estivation, para makatipid ng tubig at enerhiya hanggang bumalik ang ulan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buhaton sa suso panahon sa grabeng tinig-init?

Sa panahon sa grabeng tinig-init, ang pipila ka mananap sama sa suso mosulod sa katulad sa pagkatulog nga gitawag estivation, aron matipigan ang tubig ug enerhiya hangtod mobalik ang ulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The tiny Etruscan shrew's heart can beat over 1,000 times a minute
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: A record heartbeat rate is trivia, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en:
Which animal's heart beats fastest?

The tiny Etruscan shrew's heart can beat over 1,000 times a minute — one of the fastest heartbeats of any animal!
copy.tl:
Aling hayop ang may pinakamabilis na tibok ng puso?

Ang puso ng Etruscan shrew ay maaaring tumibok ng mahigit 1,000 beses kada minuto — isa sa pinakamabilis sa lahat ng hayop!
copy.bis:
Unsang mananapa ang adunay pinakapaspas nga pitik sa kasingkasing?

Ang kasingkasing sa Etruscan shrew makapitik ug kapin sa 1,000 ka beses kada minuto — usa sa pinakapaspas sa tanang mananap!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It weighs about as much as a small coin -- only around two grams!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions grams as a unit of mass, but it does not teach identification or appropriate use of units in a science activity. It is a factual statement about an animal's weight, not instruction on units.

copy.en:
How tiny is the Etruscan shrew?

It weighs about as much as a small coin -- only around two grams!
copy.tl:
Gaano kaliit ang Etruscan shrew?

Ang timbang niya ay halos kasinggaan lang ng isang maliit na barya -- mga dalawang gramo lang!
copy.bis:
Unsa kagamay ang Etruscan shrew?

Ang iyang gibug-aton hapit sama ra kagaan sa usa ka gamay nga sinsilyo -- mga duha lang ka gramo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: past eruptions sent flows down those exact same paths
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why certain barangays evacuate first by noting that past eruptions sent flows down the same paths. This touches on predictability of eruption impacts, but it does not discuss patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years or involve discussion with family/community members as the competency requires.

copy.en:
Why do some barangays always evacuate first?

Low valleys and river barangays are often asked to leave first! This is because past eruptions sent flows down those exact same paths.
copy.tl:
Bakit laging unang aalis ang ilang mga barangay?

Ang mga mabababang lambak at river barangays ay kadalasang unang pinapaalis! Dahil dati nang mga eruptions ang nagdala ng flows sa parehong paths.
copy.bis:
Nganong kanunay unang mopahawa ang pipila ka barangay?

Ang mga ubos nga kapatagan ug barangay sa suba kanunay unang gipahawa! Kay ang mga nag-agi nga eruptions nagpadala ug flows sa parehas nga agianan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the biggest blast often comes later
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a general pattern (biggest blast later) and evacuation behavior, but does not discuss patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years, nor involve family/community discussion or assessment of predictability. It is only tangentially related to volcanic activity and safety.

copy.en: When volcano alerts rise, people leave early! This life-saving pattern works because the biggest blast often comes later.
copy.tl: Kapag tumataas ang alerto, umalis nang maaga ang mga tao! Nakakaligtas ito ng buhay dahil ang pinakamalakas na pagsabog ay maaaring dumating mamaya.
copy.bis: Kung mosaka ang alert, mi-evacuate daan ang mga tawo! Nakaluwas kini og kinabuhi kay ang pinakadako nga pagsabog basin moabot unya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: organisms are spread out in a regular pattern
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a population distribution pattern and mentions competition for space/resources, but it does not teach the distinction between biotic and abiotic factors or name examples such as light, water, temperature, or soil type.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: often because they compete for space or resources
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: Competition is an interaction between living things, but the card only states a cause of uniform distribution; it does not explain how interactions bring good or harm to the living things involved.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: often because they compete for space or resources
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: Competition for resources relates to dependence on the environment, but the card does not explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs.

copy.en: In uniform distribution, organisms are spread out in a regular pattern, often because they compete for space or resources.
copy.tl: Sa uniform distribution, ang mga organismo ay kumakalat nang may regular na pattern, kadalasan dahil nag-aagawan sila sa espasyo o resources.
copy.bis: Sa uniform distribution, ang mga organismo nagkatag sa regular nga pattern, sagad tungod kay nag-indigay sila sa espasyo o resources.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is the exact number of vibrations per second an object makes when you tap it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines natural frequency as vibrations per second, which touches on the concept of frequency, but the competency requires researching using secondary sources to identify how wave properties (amplitude, frequency, wavelength, velocity) are described. The card does not address research, secondary sources, or the other wave properties, and only gives a single informal definition without connecting it to wave terminology or properties.

copy.en:
Did you know every object has a secret rhythm?

It’s called natural frequency! It is the exact number of vibrations per second an object makes when you tap it.
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba na may sariling ritmo ang bawat bagay?

Tinatawag itong natural frequency! Ito ang bilang ng pag-uga ng isang bagay kada segundo kapag tinapik mo ito.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang matag butang adunay kaugalingong ritmo?

Gitawag kini nga natural frequency! Kini ang gidaghanon sa pag-uyog sa butang matag segundo kung tapikon nimo kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Biological evidence like fossils
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses evidence for Pangaea (fossils, matching rocks, glacial deposits, seafloor spreading), which is unrelated to the G3-L-2 competency about observing and describing differences between living and non-living things in the local environment. The content is Earth science, not living vs non-living classification.

copy.en:
What kinds of evidence support the existence of Pangaea?

Biological evidence like fossils, geological evidence like matching rocks, climate evidence like glacial deposits, and seafloor spreading!
copy.tl:
Anong mga uri ng ebidensya ang sumusuporta sa pag-iral ng Pangaea?

Biological evidence tulad ng fossils, geological evidence tulad ng magkatugmang bato, climate evidence tulad ng glacial deposits, at seafloor spreading!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga klase sa ebidensya ang nagsuporta sa paglungtad sa Pangaea?

Biological evidence sama sa fossils, geological evidence sama sa magkatugmang bato, climate evidence sama sa glacial deposits, ug seafloor spreading!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Charles Darwin explained it by natural selection.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change
assignedReviews.reason: The card only identifies Darwin as the person who explained evolution by natural selection. It does not describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change, nor does it use secondary sources. The content is topically related but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Charles Darwin explained it by natural selection.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions natural selection but does not discuss important concepts in theories of evolution such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, or adaptation. It only names the proponent, so it does not directly support the discussion required by the competency.

copy.en:
Who explained evolution through natural selection?

Charles Darwin explained it by natural selection.
copy.tl:
Sino ang nagpaliwanag ng ebolusyon sa natural na seleksyon?

Si Charles Darwin ang nagpaliwanag nito sa pamamagitan ng natural na seleksyon.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang nagpasabot sa ebolusyon pinaagi sa natural nga seleksyon?

Si Charles Darwin ang nagpasabot sa ebolusyon pinaagi sa natural nga seleksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It happens when the environment changes and a species' traits are no longer enough to survive and reproduce there.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes extinction as a result of environmental change and insufficient traits, which touches on the idea of differential survival but does not name or describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change, nor does it involve secondary sources.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most species that ever lived on Earth are already extinct.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that extinction occurs when environmental change makes a species' traits insufficient, but it does not discuss threats to biodiversity or how those threats lead to extinction, and it does not support a class discussion of biodiversity threats.

copy.en: Most species that ever lived on Earth are already extinct. It happens when the environment changes and a species' traits are no longer enough to survive and reproduce there.
copy.tl: Karamihan sa mga species na nabuhay sa Earth ay lipol na. Nangyayari ito kapag nagbago ang kapaligiran at hindi na sapat ang katangian ng species para mabuhay at magparami roon.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa mga species nga nabuhi sa Yuta napuo na. Mahitabo kini kon mabag-o ang palibot ug dili na igo ang kinaiya sa species aron mabuhi ug manganak didto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they contain tiny bits of gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card names gold, silver, and copper but does not identify their properties or their uses in the local community. It only states that these metals are present in e-waste and can be recovered by recycling.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: recycling them recovers valuable metals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions recycling as a way to recover metals, but it does not demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, nor does it teach reusing, disposing of excess oil, or recycling paper, plastic, or glass as the competency requires.

copy.en: Old cellphones and computers are called "e-waste," and they contain tiny bits of gold, silver, and copper — so recycling them recovers valuable metals!
copy.tl: Ang lumang cellphone at computer ay tinatawag na "e-waste," at may laman silang maliliit na piraso ng ginto, pilak, at tanso — kaya ang pag-recycle nito ay nakababawi ng mahahalagang metal!
copy.bis: Ang daang cellphone ug computer gitawag og "e-waste," ug adunay sulod nga gagmay nga tipik sa bulawan, plata, ug tumbaga — busa ang pag-recycle niini makabawi sa mahalon nga metal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oxygen, water, gold, carbon dioxide, and carbon are examples of pure substances.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches examples of pure substances (a chemistry concept), not the basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Water, salt, and gold are pure substances, meaning each one has a fixed composition and is made of only one type of particle.
copy.tl: Ang tubig, asin, at ginto ay mga pure substances, ibig sabihin bawat isa ay may nakapirming komposisyon at gawa sa iisang uri lang ng particle.
copy.bis: Ang tubig, asin, ug bulawan kay mga pure substances, nagpasabot nga ang matag usa adunay pirmi nga komposisyon ug gihimo sa usa lang ka klase sa particle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: muscles around it get weak, so gentle exercise helps rebuild strength
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions muscles weakening and exercise, but it does not describe how the muscular system works (e.g., contraction, movement, coordination with skeletal system). It is a health-related fact about muscle recovery, not an explanation of the system's function.

copy.en: While a limb is in a cast, the muscles around it get weak, so gentle exercise helps rebuild strength once it's removed.
copy.tl: Habang nakakabit ang cast, humihina ang kalamnan sa paligid nito, kaya may banayad na ehersisyo para bumalik ang lakas pagkatanggal.
copy.bis: Samtang naa sa cast, moluya ang kaunoran sa palibot, mao nga adunay hinay nga ehersisyo aron mobalik ang kusog human kuhaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: while it's still digesting your food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a health tip about waiting after eating before exercise, mentioning digestion only in passing. It does not describe how the digestive system or any other body system works, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why wait before exercising after a meal?

If you move too soon after eating, your tummy may hurt while it's still digesting your food — so it's best to wait a little while first.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangang maghintay bago mag-ehersisyo pagkakain?

Kung agad kang gagalaw pagkatapos kumain, baka sumakit ang tiyan mo habang tinutunaw pa ang pagkain — kaya mas mabuting maghintay muna ng kaunti.
copy.bis:
Ngano kinahanglan maghulat una mag-ehersisyo human mokaon?

Kon molihok dayon ka human mokaon, basin masakit ang imong tiyan samtang gitunaw pa ang pagkaon — mao nga mas maayo nga maghulat una og gamay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We lose water through sweat, so we need to drink while exercising.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water as something we need, but it is specifically about drinking water during exercise, not about identifying the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). It does not teach the general concept of basic needs or provide examples across living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We lose water through sweat, so we need to drink while exercising.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that water is one of the basic needs of plants and animals
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about human water loss and rehydration during exercise, not about recognizing water as a basic need of plants and animals. It does not address plants or animals generally, and the context is exercise, not the fundamental need for water.

copy.en:
Why drink water when we exercise?

We lose water through sweat, so we need to drink while exercising.
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat uminom ng tubig kapag nag-eehersisyo?

Nawawalan tayo ng tubig sa pawis, kaya kailangan nating uminom habang nag-eehersisyo.
copy.bis:
Nganong kinahanglan moinom og tubig kung mag-ehersisyo?

Mawad-an ta ug tubig pinaagi sa singot, mao nga kinahanglan ta moinom samtang mag-ehersisyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has 78% nitrogen, 16% oxygen, and 4% carbon dioxide!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the composition of exhaled air, not air in general, and omits water vapor, which is a required component in the competency. It only shares the vocabulary of gases and does not directly teach that air is a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's way more CO2 and less oxygen than the air we breathe in.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a difference between inhaled and exhaled air, which is tangentially related to respiration, but it does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor does it identify raw materials and products. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
What's inside the air we breathe out?

It has 78% nitrogen, 16% oxygen, and 4% carbon dioxide! That's way more CO2 and less oxygen than the air we breathe in.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nasa hangin na ating hinihinga palabas?

May 78% nitrogen, 16% oxygen, at 4% carbon dioxide ito! Mas maraming CO2 at mas kaunting oxygen kaysa sa hinihinga natin.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang sulod sa hangin nga atong ginaginhawa palabas?

Adunay 78% nitrogen, 16% oxygen, ug 4% carbon dioxide! Mas daghang CO2 ug mas gamayng oxygen kaysa sa atong ginaginhawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When air inside a bottle is heated, it expands!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes that heated air expands and can inflate a balloon. It does not mention particles, their motion, spacing, attraction, or the particle-level explanation of expansion with heat, so it does not directly teach the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When air inside a bottle is heated, it expands!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The competency concerns changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes, with examples like burning wood or coal. The card shows expansion of air when heated, which is a temperature-related change, but it does not describe changes in material properties in the sense of the competency's examples or content.

copy.en: When air inside a bottle is heated, it expands! This can even blow up a balloon stretched over the bottle's mouth.
copy.tl: Kapag pinainit ang hangin sa loob ng bote, lumalawak ito! Maaari pa nitong palakihin ang lobong nakatakip sa bunganga nito.
copy.bis: Kon init-an ang hangin sa sulod sa botelya, mosangkad kini! Mahimo pa kining mopadako sa lobo nga nakatabon sa baba sa botelya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Materials change their chemical properties when exposed to heat, bacteria, oxygen, and other chemicals.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about chemical changes in materials, not about observing or recording weather changes. It does not support the G3-E-4 competency on weather patterns.

copy.en: Materials change their chemical properties when exposed to heat, bacteria, oxygen, and other chemicals.
copy.tl: Ang mga materyales ay nagbabago ng kanilang chemical properties kapag na-expose sa init, bacteria, oxygen, at iba pang mga kemikal.
copy.bis: Ang mga materyales mausab ang ilang kemikal nga properties kon ma-expose sa init, bacteria, oxygen, ug uban pang mga kemikal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When an animal is extinct, it means every single one of its kind has died — and it will never come back.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines extinction, which is necessary background for discussing how threats lead to extinction, but it does not discuss threats, biodiversity, or involve a class discussion as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When an animal is extinct, it means every single one of its kind has died — and it will never come back.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines extinction but does not classify Philippine animals/plants as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable, nor does it use secondary sources. The concept is related but not directly supporting the classification skill.

copy.en:
What does 'extinct' mean?

When an animal is extinct, it means every single one of its kind has died — and it will never come back.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng extinct?

Kapag sinabing extinct ang isang hayop, ibig sabihin lahat ng uri nito ay namatay na at hindi na ito babalik kailanman.
copy.bis:
Unsay ipasabot sa extinct?

Kung ang usa ka mananap giingong extinct, buot ipasabot nga ang tanang matang niini namatay na ug dili na gyud mobalik.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An extinct species has died out completely
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines what extinction means, which is necessary background for discussing how threats to biodiversity lead to extinction, but it does not address threats to biodiversity or the causal link to extinction. The competency also requires a class discussion, which the card does not provide.

copy.en:
What does it mean when a species is extinct?

An extinct species has died out completely — not even one is left alive anywhere, and it can never come back.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng extinct?

Ang extinct na species ay tuluyan nang naubos — wala nang kahit isang buhay na natitira kahit saan, at hindi na ito maibabalik.
copy.bis:
Unsay buot ipasabot sa extinct?

Ang extinct nga species nahurot na sa hingpit — wala nay bisan usa nga buhi bisan asa, ug dili na kini mabalik.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A species is extinct when not one single living member of it remains anywhere on Earth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines extinction, which is necessary background for discussing how threats lead to extinction, but it does not address threats to biodiversity or involve a class discussion as required by the competency.

copy.en:
What does 'extinct' mean?

A species is extinct when not one single living member of it remains anywhere on Earth.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng extinct?

Extinct o lipol na ang isang species kapag wala nang kahit isang buhay na miyembro nito sa buong mundo.
copy.bis:
Unsay buot ipasabot sa extinct?

Lipol na ang usa ka species kon wala nay bisan usa ka buhi nga sakop niini bisan asa sa kalibotan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An extinct animal is gone for good, but an endangered animal still has a few left that can be saved before it disappears.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines extinct and endangered but does not classify any Philippine species as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable, nor does it use secondary resources.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An extinct animal is gone for good, but an endangered animal still has a few left that can be saved before it disappears.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not discuss threats to biodiversity or extinction, and there is no class discussion component.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An extinct animal is gone for good, but an endangered animal still has a few left that can be saved before it disappears.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies that endangered animals can be saved, but it does not explicitly teach the need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive.

copy.en:
What's the difference between extinct and endangered?

An extinct animal is gone for good, but an endangered animal still has a few left that can be saved before it disappears.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng extinct at endangered?

Ang extinct na hayop ay wala na talaga, pero ang endangered ay kakaunti pa lang ang natitira at maaari pang iligtas.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang kalahian sa extinct ug endangered?

Ang extinct nga hayop wala na gyud, apan ang endangered gamay na lang ang nahibilin ug maluwas pa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 'endangered' means a species needs protection, while 'critically endangered' means it faces an even higher risk of dying out soon.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the general IUCN meanings of endangered and critically endangered, which is useful background for classifying species, but it does not classify Philippine animals or plants into these categories as the competency requires.

copy.en:
What's the difference between endangered and critically endangered?

The IUCN classifies threatened species — 'endangered' means a species needs protection, while 'critically endangered' means it faces an even higher risk of dying out soon.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng endangered at critically endangered?

Inuuri ng IUCN ang mga nanganganib na species — nangangailangan ng proteksyon ang 'endangered', habang mas mataas ang panganib ng pagkalipol sa malapit na hinaharap ang 'critically endangered'.
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa endangered ug critically endangered?

copy.en:
What does 'extinction' mean?

Extinction means every member of a species has died and none can return — once a species is gone, it is gone forever.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng extinction?

Ang extinction ay nangangahulugang namatay na ang lahat ng miyembro ng isang species at wala nang makakabalik — kapag nawala na ang isang species, permanente na itong nawala.
copy.bis:
Unsay buot ipasabot sa extinction?

Ang extinction nagpasabot nga namatay na ang tanang miyembro sa usa ka species ug walay makabalik — kon mawala na ang usa ka species, permanente na kining nawala.

copy.en:
What does extinction mean?

Extinction happens when every last member of a species dies out and none are left — most species that ever lived on Earth, like the dinosaurs, are now extinct.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng extinction?

Nangyayari ang extinction kapag tuluyang nawala ang lahat ng miyembro ng isang species; karamihan sa mga species na dating nabuhay sa Earth, tulad ng dinosaur, ay extinct na ngayon.
copy.bis:
Unsay buot ipasabot sa extinction?

Mahitabo ang extinction kung ang tanang miyembro sa usa ka species mawala hangtod walay mahibilin; kadaghanan sa mga species nga nabuhi sa Earth, sama sa dinosaur, extinct na karon.

copy.en:
What does extinction really mean?

Extinction happens when every member of an animal or plant kind dies out, so none are ever left on Earth again.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng pagkalipol?

Nangyayari ang pagkalipol kapag namatay na ang lahat ng miyembro ng isang uri ng hayop o halaman, kaya wala na itong matitira sa mundo magpakailanman.
copy.bis:
Unsay buot ipasabot sa pagkapuo?

Mahitabo ang pagkapuo kon mamatay na ang tanang sakop sa usa ka matang sa mananap o tanom, mao nga wala na kini mahabilin sa kalibotan hangtod sa kahangtoran.

How does climate change affect weather?

Climate change makes some storms stronger! It also brings more intense heat and droughts to different places.

Paano nakakaapekto ang climate change sa panahon?

Nagpapalakas ang climate change ng ilang bagyo! Nagdudulot din ito ng mas matinding init at tagtuyot sa iba't ibang lugar.
